item.title: Hill Anti-Demolition Quest Advances
item.description: The state Historic Preservation Council voted unanimously Wednesday to ask the Office of the Attorney General to stop a local health center from tearing down a dilapidated building on Howard Avenue. item.title: Safe-Streets “Quick Build”? Let’s Goffe About It
item.description: The Elicker administration has launched a new effort to redesign six blocks of Goffe Street using a slate of “quick-build” traffic-calming and placemaking changes -- with the goal of testing updates on the street before committing to more costly permanent construction. The post Safe-Streets “Quick Build”? Let’s Goffe About It appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: School-By-School Funding To Mirror State Pitch
item.description: Next fiscal year, every New Haven school will receive a small amount of additional money from the district based on the number of students receiving special education or multilingual learning services -- as the city presses the state to make a similar commitment in its own school-funding formula. The post School-By-School Funding To Mirror State Pitch appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: City Union Election Challenged, Rerun Canceled
item.description: One of the city's largest municipal unions has canceled a "rerun" leadership election that had been scheduled to take place on Friday -- after a previous president successfully challenged the current president's reelection last October. item.title: City Apologizes For Towing 58 Cars On Short Notice
item.description: The Elicker administration has promised to reimburse towing fees and cancel tickets for all 58 cars that were towed from five Wooster Square blocks Tuesday morning -- after the city didn't give residents, including the neighborhood's alder, enough time to prepare for a snow-removal-related parking ban.
